R4F-bear-drive-0001.name: By Sunset Creek
R4F-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R4F-bear-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on Sunset Mainline (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2006 (20 years old), 60 m NE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2021 (fire K21809), 250 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Sunset Creek 60 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Mica Creek, about 68 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.63214, -119.03087, pull off on Sunset Mainline (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 60 m SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 0 m, about 5 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-42, Region 3. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-10, closures 2026-10-16.
R4F-bear-drive-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 3-42: about 181 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.12 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.1 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R4F-grouse-drive-0002.name: 180 m S of Sunset Creek
R4F-grouse-drive-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
3 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
14 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

seasonRows.notes: youth only: hunters under 18 (page footnote); New, printed green
MU 3-42 is not listed in the Region 3 sharp tailed grouse rows (my reading of the table).

plan: Drive: from Mica Creek, about 71 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.64099, -119.08549, pull off on 1600.02 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk or drive slowly: the Sunset Mainline stretch, 4.1 km one way. About 81 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-42, Region 3. Season: grouse Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 34, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-10, closures 2026-10-16.

Burn from 2021 (fire K21809), 40 m NE: browse.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

seasonRows.notes: Bag 1; spike fork bulls: antlers must accompany the species licence (page footnote)
